title: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy)
indication: NCCP00794a covers adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease. The NCCP entry specifies ECOG 0–1. Broader European licensed indications must be checked separately against the applicable Irish regimen and reimbursement pathway.

sources.title: NCCP00794 v3, reviewed 4 March 2025; checked 20 October 2026
Trodelvy EU Summary of Product Characteristics, sections 4.2–4.6 and 5.1; checked 20 October 2026
Bardia et al. Sacituzumab Govitecan in Metastatic Triple-Negative Breast Cancer. NEJM 2021;384:1529–1541

schedule: Two treatment visits in each three-week cycle: Day 1, then Day 8. There is no planned infusion on Day 15. The next cycle starts after Day 21 if the team confirms it is appropriate.
baseline: Before the first treatment: full blood count, kidney and liver blood tests, glucose and electrolytes including magnesium, calcium and phosphate. Pregnancy testing is needed where relevant. ECG is added if clinically indicated. The team checks infection, medicines, previous low blood counts and whether preventive G-CSF injections are appropriate.
ongoing: Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle; the neutrophil count must also meet the separate Day 8 threshold before that infusion. Glucose and the listed electrolytes are checked every second cycle. Pregnancy testing is repeated before each cycle where relevant. Review diarrhoea, hydration, nausea, oral intake, fever and infection before each infusion. Scans follow the individual response-assessment plan.
clinical_notes: NCCP00794a is later-line unresectable/metastatic TNBC. Do not import current EU HR-positive, first-line or pembrolizumab-combination indications without the appropriate separate NCCP/reimbursement mapping.
Day 1 ANC threshold is ≥1.5 ×10⁹/L; Day 8 is ≥1.0 ×10⁹/L. An isolated ANC <1.0 can trigger a hold without a day; 1.0–<1.5 requires day context rather than a false clearance.

NCCP high-emetic-risk prophylaxis must cover BOTH Day 1 and Day 8. The suggested dexamethasone 12 mg infusion premedicine also provides antiemetic cover; reconcile with the selected high-risk script to prevent duplication.

NCCP suggested infusion premedicines: paracetamol 1 g PO 60 minutes beforehand; chlorphenamine 10 mg IV, famotidine 20 mg IV and dexamethasone 12 mg PO 30 minutes beforehand. Product availability, contraindications and local prescriptions must be checked.

Primary G-CSF should be considered from cycle 1 for increased-risk patients in the current EU SmPC. Product and timing must account for Day 1 and Day 8; do not automatically generate a single generic pegfilgrastim date.

NCCP advises considering a lower initial dose for known UGT1A1*28 homozygosity and possible escalation based on cycle-1 tolerance, but gives no fixed starting reduction. The EU SmPC recommends close monitoring and does not require routine genotype testing when status is unknown. Do not re-escalate a dose previously reduced because of adverse reactions.

NCCP Table 1 repeats 25% dose reduction at the second severe non-neutropenic event, whereas the current EU SmPC gives a 10→7.5→5 mg/kg ladder. The second-event output requires Consultant/pharmacy reconciliation and suppresses automatic numeric dosing.

NCCP Table 2 predicts no renal/hepatic adjustment across broad impairment bands. EU SmPC advises avoiding use when bilirubin >1.5×ULN or AST/ALT >3×ULN without liver metastases or >5×ULN with metastases, and notes absent severe/end-stage renal data. These differences are explicit in the assessment output.

NCCP contains >48-hour and >3-week toxicity-duration rules that differ from the current EU algorithm. Persisting severe toxicity must not be treated by merely calculating a reduced dose; recovery and source reconciliation are required.

NCCP's high-dose loperamide schedule is 4 mg initially then 2 mg every two hours, continued 12 hours after the last liquid stool and never beyond 48 consecutive hours at these doses because of ileus risk. The patient-facing page should direct to an individually prescribed local oncology plan rather than print an unsupervised automatic prescription. Assess infectious causes, fever, blood, severe pain and dehydration promptly.
Scan timing is Consultant-plan-specific; no universal three-month CT or tumour-marker schedule is specified in NCCP00794. Routine ECG/echo/DXA should not be added merely to fill a timeline.
Software source reconciliation and 143 scenario/structure checks do not constitute independent Consultant or oncology-pharmacy validation.

evidence.title: ASCENT — Bardia et al., NEJM 2021
evidence.population: Randomised open-label phase III trial, 529 patients with previously treated metastatic TNBC. The primary efficacy population comprised 468 patients without baseline brain metastases; ECOG was 0–1.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in the population without baseline brain metastases.
evidence.interpretation: In the primary population, median PFS was 5.6 versus 1.7 months (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.32–0.52) and median OS was 12.1 versus 6.7 months (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.38–0.59) with sacituzumab versus physician-choice chemotherapy. Response was 35% versus 5%.
evidence.limitations: The primary analysis excluded baseline brain metastases; the overall-population estimates differ. Open-label design, selected trial fitness and previous-treatment requirements limit extrapolation. Group medians do not predict an individual patient's benefit. This trial does not establish eligibility for every broader current EU indication.
